headline: The first bad quarter
body: Revenue missed by 6%. The stock is down 22% in a day.

options.label: Reassure the market with a bold forecast
options.detail: The price recovers now. You'll need to actually hit the number.
options.storyHeadline: Talked the market back up with a bold forecast
options.mentorHint: The price comes back today on a promise. Someone is going to remember you made it.

options.label: Say it plainly and take the hit
options.detail: The price stays down for a while. Nobody catches you overpromising.
options.storyHeadline: Took the hit and said it plainly

options.label: Announce a buyback
options.detail: Company cash props the price up artificially.
options.storyHeadline: Announced a buyback to support the price

headline: The lockup expires
body: For the first time, you're actually allowed to sell.

options.label: Sell 10% of your stake
options.detail: Real money. The market reads it as a signal, and it isn't a good one.
options.storyHeadline: Sold 10% the day the lockup expired
options.mentorHint: The cash is real. So is every headline that starts with 'founder dumps shares.'

options.label: Sell 2% quietly
options.detail: Barely anyone notices.
options.storyHeadline: Sold a small slice quietly

options.label: Sell nothing
options.detail: Everything you have stays exactly as liquid as it was yesterday: not very.
options.storyHeadline: Held everything at the lockup expiry

headline: An activist arrives
body: A fund has bought 6% of the company and published a letter about your leadership.

options.label: Meet them and concede something
options.detail: They go quiet. You lose a plan you cared about.
options.storyHeadline: Conceded ground to an activist investor

options.label: Fight publicly
options.detail: A real bet on whether the market backs you or them.
options.storyHeadline: Fought an activist investor publicly

gamble.winText: The market backs you. They go quiet.
gamble.loseText: A two-year proxy battle, and you're already tired.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Won a public fight with an activist investor
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Lost a public fight with an activist investor

options.label: Buy them out at a premium
options.detail: Expensive. Also over, immediately.
options.storyHeadline: Bought out an activist investor at a premium

headline: The board wants a professional CEO
body: They think the company has outgrown you. They might be right.

options.label: Step aside, stay as chairman
options.detail: The company does better without you in the way. You stop deciding.
options.storyHeadline: Stepped aside for a professional CEO

options.label: Refuse
options.detail: You're still running this. They notice.
options.storyHeadline: Refused to step aside for a professional CEO

options.label: Offer a two-year deadline on the numbers
options.detail: Hit them, and this goes away. Miss, and it gets much worse.
options.storyHeadline: Bet the board on hitting a two-year target

gamble.winText: You hit the numbers. Nobody mentions it again.
gamble.loseText: You missed, and now it's not really a question anymore.
gamble.winStoryHeadline: Hit the numbers and silenced the board
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: Missed the numbers the board gave you

headline: A market crash that has nothing to do with you
body: The index fell 30%. Your business is unchanged. Your paper wealth just halved anyway.

options.label: Announce a buyback
options.detail: Company cash props up the price, partially.
options.storyHeadline: Bought back shares through a market crash

options.label: Ignore it and keep working
options.detail: The correct answer, which is why it's boring.
options.storyHeadline: Kept working through a market crash that had nothing to do with the business
options.mentorHint: Nothing about the business changed today. The number attached to it did anyway.

headline: You could buy it all back
body: Take it private yourself. It would cost everything you don't have.

options.label: Take it private
options.detail: Borrow the rest of the company back from every other shareholder. You own it all again, heavily indebted.
options.storyHeadline: Took the company private again, heavily indebted
options.mentorHint: You own all of it again. The bank owns a claim on all of it too, until the loan is gone.

options.label: Stay public
options.detail: The board, the quarterly numbers, the analysts — all of it, still.
options.storyHeadline: Decided to stay public rather than buy the company back

headline: An analyst downgrades you
body: One influential note, and the tone in every headline changes for a week.

options.label: Respond publicly
options.detail: You make your case. It half-works.
options.storyHeadline: Responded publicly to an analyst downgrade

options.label: Say nothing
options.detail: It passes, the way most weeks do.
options.storyHeadline: Said nothing after an analyst downgrade

headline: You're being added to an index
body: Every fund that tracks it now has to own you, whether they like the business or not.

options.label: Ride the wave
options.detail: Forced buying pushes the price up on its own.
options.storyHeadline: Rode an index-inclusion rally

options.label: Sell into the strength
options.detail: The price is up for reasons that have nothing to do with you. Take some of it.
options.storyHeadline: Sold shares into an index-inclusion rally

headline: The numbers need restating
body: Nothing criminal. Just wrong, in a way that makes last year's results look better than they were.

options.label: Come clean immediately
options.detail: It's bad. It's also over quickly.
options.storyHeadline: Came clean immediately about an accounting restatement

options.label: Let the lawyers manage the story
options.detail: Slower, and you don't fully control how it ends.
options.storyHeadline: Let the lawyers manage an accounting restatement

gamble.loseText: It doesn't stay contained. It unravels the whole thing.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: An accounting restatement unraveled the company

headline: The vesting cliff hits
body: Four years in, right on schedule, a chunk of your earliest employees are fully vested — and gone within the month.

options.label: Refresh everyone's grants early
options.detail: Expensive, and most of them stay.
options.storyHeadline: Refreshed equity grants to keep the team after vesting
options.mentorHint: The dilution is the visible cost. The alternative is watching four years of institutional knowledge walk out the door at once.

options.label: Let it happen
options.detail: They earned it. You start over with whoever stays.
options.storyHeadline: Lost staff to the first vesting cliff

headline: A short-seller publishes a report on you
body: Ninety pages, some of it wrong, some of it uncomfortably not.

options.label: Rebut it point by point
options.detail: A real bet on whether the market believes the rebuttal.
options.storyHeadline: Rebutted a short-seller report point by point

gamble.winText: The rebuttal holds up. The report ages badly instead.
gamble.loseText: One of the uncomfortable parts turns out to be true.
gamble.loseStoryHeadline: A short-seller report turned out to have a point

options.label: Say nothing and let it pass
options.detail: Most of these fade on their own, eventually.
options.storyHeadline: Said nothing about a short-seller report

headline: Investors want to end your control structure
body: Your shares vote more than theirs do. A growing number of them would like that to stop.

options.label: Keep the control structure
options.detail: You stay firmly in charge. Some investors stay firmly annoyed.
options.storyHeadline: Kept a dual-class share structure against investor pressure

options.label: Simplify for investors
options.detail: One share, one vote. Cleaner governance, less of it yours.
options.storyHeadline: Gave up dual-class shares to simplify governance

headline: You could pay a dividend
body: The company throws off more cash than it needs. Some investors have been asking.

options.label: Pay it
options.detail: A real signal of stability. Also real cash, gone quarterly, from now on.
options.storyHeadline: Paid the company's first dividend
options.mentorHint: A dividend is a promise to keep paying it. The market notices a lot more when you stop than when you start.

options.label: Reinvest instead
options.detail: Slower to reward shareholders, faster to grow.
options.storyHeadline: Reinvested instead of paying a dividend
